Hi Alan — thanks for the clear list. See our responses below; I'm attaching a filled copy of your questionnaire and a simple retention diagram. If you want any of the answers tightened into a single-line statement for your report, let me know.

1) Region / residency
- Default hosting regions: US customers are served from us-central1 (primary) and optionally us-east1 for redundancy; EU customers are served from eu-west1.
- Account-level region pinning: yes. For hosted API customers we offer account-scoped region pinning (select a primary region) which pins storage and compute to that region for all request/response data and cache shards. Please note: cross-region backups may still occur for disaster recovery unless you select our geo-fence-only plan (available on Dedicated/Private).

2) Default retention periods
- Raw request/response payloads (input text and model outputs): retained for 45 days by default to support debugging, abuse detection, and short-term replay. Customers may opt into shorter retention (ephemeral mode) at account level; retention = 0 days (no persistent storage) for requests that do not require troubleshooting.
- Aggregated telemetry and metrics (latency, token counts, billing aggregates): retained for 365 days.
- Audit logs (control plane events, auth attempts): retained for 1 year.
- Cached KV/prefix caches and per-request ephemeral caches: kept in-memory and on local SSDs for at most 12 hours by default; these caches are not durable storage for customer data and are evicted frequently.
- Backups and snapshots of model serving nodes: retained for 14 days in the primary region; cold backups used for DR may be retained up to 30 days and are subject to deletion windows described below.

3) Account-level deletion / erasure process and timelines
- How we process requests: Submit a verified erasure request via your account owner or through our support portal (link below). Upon verification we: 1) mark all associated primary objects for immediate deletion, 2) scrub indexes/meta, 3) remove references from caches.
- Timing expectations: primary storage purge typically completes within 7 days from request acceptance. In-memory caches and live replicas are cleared within 48 hours.
- Backups and replicated copies: because some backup systems are immutably-scheduled, complete removal from all cold backups can take up to 30 days. We will provide a deletion ticket and a statement confirming the completion of each phase.
- Exceptions: legal holds or subpoenas may delay purges; we will notify your security team if any such boundary applies.

4) Embeddings and derived artifacts
- By default, Redwood does NOT persist embeddings or derived artifacts from hosted API calls unless a customer explicitly opts in (for features such as semantic search or vector DB hosting). If you enable embedding persistence we retain embeddings per your retention policy (default 90 days) and will remove them on erasure requests per the timelines above.

5) Minimizing residency / ephemeral mode
- Ephemeral mode (account-level toggle): requests are processed in-memory and are not written to persistent storage. Useful for high-sensitivity workloads; reduces debugging capability.
- Transit encryption: all traffic is TLS 1.3 in transit and encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS integration) available for Dedicated and Private.

Additional notes and compliance artifacts
- We can provide a DPA and our SOC 2 report on request; see linked artifacts.
- Auditability: we record an auditable erasure ticket and provide a deletion completion notice.
